To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the M50 latency of children with ASD was significantly longer than that of age-matched TD children.
the auditory evoked response is modulated by white mater structure and neurochemical activity in typically developing children and children with ASD.
the auditory evoked neuromagnetic response (auditory M50) latency is modulated by both white matter microstructure and GABA levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and contrasting the multiple physiological mechanisms that are involved in the efficient encoding of auditory sensory input.
the identification of brain level mechanisms that are associated with auditory information processing efficiency.

the development of new imaging techniques that are sensitive to changes in brain physiology and structure in ASD and that are capable of identifying subgroups of individuals with ASD who may be responsive to specific treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study demonstrates the importance of the white matter tracts in the transmission of auditory information from the ear to the brain and that the integrity of these tracts is compromised in children with ASD.
the auditory evoked neuromagnetic response in children with ASD is characterized by altered microstructural integrity and neurochemical function of the auditory pathway.
ASD is a heterogeneous disorder, and it is important to understand the underlying mechanisms in order to better understand the etiology of the disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ASD is not a single entity, but a heterogeneous collection of disorders that can be differentiated on the basis of their underlying brain structure and neurochemistry.
ASD is a heterogeneous disorder with respect to brain level building blocks and that the brain level building blocks are not necessarily related to behavior.

the M50 latency model can identify subpopulations within ASD with distinct underlying neurophysiologic profiles, and that these profiles can be related to underlying microstructure and neurochemistry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are multiple physiological mechanisms associated auditory processing efficiency in ASD and that these mechanisms are not all affected in all ASD.
the M50 latency is not only a function of the speed of conduction in the auditory pathway but also a function of the underlying microstructure and neurochemistry of the auditory pathway.
the auditory evoked response is a complex phenomenon that depends upon multiple physiological factors.
